questions.q:
With reference to High Court rulings in the debate on POCSO and adolescent consent, consider the following pairs:
1. Ashik Ramjali Ansari (2023), Bombay High Court : Sexual autonomy includes both the right to choose and the right to protection from aggression
2. Mohd. Rafayat Ali (2025), Delhi High Court : Consensual adolescent love, free of coercion, deserves respect
3. State v. Hitesh (2025), Delhi High Court : Consent is legally immaterial under POCSO if the victim is under 18
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Pairs 2 and 3 are interchanged: Hitesh is the ruling that treated consensual adolescent love free of coercion with respect, while Rafayat Ali restated that consent has no legal value below 18. The Delhi High Court thus appears on both sides, which is why it is argued that the Supreme Court should resolve the divide between statute and High Court rulings, leaving any lowering of the age to Parliament.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 6-8

questions.q: In the discussion on urban water reform, the '3Ps framework' refers to
questions.e: The framework calls for policy alignment across sectors, citizen participation and city-catchment cooperation. The other lists sound plausible, but 'Public, Private, Partnership' is a financing model and the rest describe engineering or tariff concerns. The point of the framework is that urban water failure is a failure of governance as well as infrastructure. It sits alongside integrated urban water management and a single city-level water authority in the way forward.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
Samiullah v. State of Bihar discussed Article 300A. Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A person cannot ordinarily approach the Supreme Court directly under Article 32 for a violation of Article 300A alone.
Statement-II: The 44th Amendment removed property from the Fundamental Rights and made it a constitutional right in Part XII.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Article 32 is the remedy for Fundamental Rights, so a person relying on Article 300A alone would ordinarily use Article 226 before a High Court. Article 300A still requires authority of law, so an executive order alone is not enough. The Court's concern was that demanding proof of mutation indirectly demanded proof of title and so curtailed the freedom to transfer property.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-23; the rest is static

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the history and law behind the Governor's address?
o: Under Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 the address was discretionary, and from April 1937 the speech was prepared in consultation with provincial ministers
Shamsher Singh (1974) held that the Governor exercises executive power independently of the Council of Ministers
The address was first prepared by ministers after the Constitution came into force, and Nabam Rebia (2016) confined this to Article 175
Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 made the address mandatory at each session, and Shamsher Singh (1974) let the Governor depart from it
questions.e: The 1935 Act said the Governor may in his discretion address the provincial legislature, and ministerial drafting began with provincial autonomy in 1937. The Constituent Assembly carried that understanding forward. Shamsher Singh treated the Governor as a constitutional head acting on ministerial advice, so the claims of independence fail. Nabam Rebia applied aid and advice to the address under both Articles 175 and 176, so it did not confine it to one.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4

questions.q:
In the debate on Finance Commission criteria, consider the following statements:
1. The income distance criterion gives larger transfers to poorer States.
2. The demographic performance criterion rewards reduction in fertility.
3. Using the 2011 population gives greater relative weight to States that reduced their fertility earlier than using the 1971 population does.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is the wrong way round: the 2011 population reflects current needs and favours States whose population grew more, while the 1971 population was used to reward population control. This is why southern States say both seats and funds can penalise them for demographic success, and why a total fertility rate-adjusted seat formula has been suggested as a way forward.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7

questions.q:
Match List-I (digital tool of Census 2027) with List-II (what it does):
List-I
A. Houselisting Block Creator
B. Census Management and Monitoring System
C. Census as a Service
D. Self-Enumeration Portal
List-II
1. Clean, machine-readable database that ministries can query for planning
2. Satellite-based web-mapping application for Charge Officers
3. Progress tracking by supervisors and district officers
4. Questionnaire completed by citizens themselves on a secure platform
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Block Creator lets Charge Officers draw digital enumeration blocks on satellite-based maps. The monitoring system is the supervisory dashboard. Census as a Service is about using the data afterwards, since it gives ministries a queryable database for evidence-based planning. The Self-Enumeration Portal is the citizen-facing tool. The trap is mixing up the citizen portal with the data service, because both sound public-facing. Asking who uses each tool separates them.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Striking down of the 'Single Directive' in Vineet Narain v. Union of India
2. Insertion of Section 17A in the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
3. Insertion of Section 6A in the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act
4. Striking down of Section 6A in Subramanian Swamy v. Director, CBI
Select the correct order:
questions.e: The order is Vineet Narain (late 1990s), Section 6A (2003), its striking down (2014) and Section 17A (2018). Each time, a prior-approval filter was struck down and later returned in a new form, which is why Justice Nagarathna called Section 17A 'old wine in a new bottle'. The magazines give different years for Vineet Narain, but the order does not change.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6

questions.q:
With reference to land records reforms, consider the following statements:
1. Karnataka's Bhoomi and KAVERI platforms link records of rights with registration.
2. The Supreme Court in Samiullah suggested blockchain for land records.
3. The proposed Registration Bill, 2025 expands registering authorities' power to decide title disputes.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the Bill keeps the distinction by limiting registering authorities' powers. Blockchain would hold one block per parcel with its full history, but it depends on accurate initial data and legal alignment, so digitisation alone will not fix the problem. In Bihar, mutation and survey processes are incomplete, so many sellers could not obtain the records the rules demanded.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-23

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Palermo Protocol is correct?
o: It is a protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which India has signed but not ratified
It supplements the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime, and India ratified it in May 2011
It defines trafficking only by reference to cross-border movement of adults
It supplements the UN Convention against Corruption, which India ratified in 2011
questions.e: The Protocol supplements the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime. The confusion with UNCAC is natural, because India ratified that treaty in 2011 as well. India signed the Protocol in 2002 and ratified it in May 2011. It covers recruitment, transport, transfer, harbouring or receipt of a child for exploitation, so it is not limited to adults or to border crossing, and it is not linked to the Child Rights Convention.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11; parent convention checked with UNODC

questions.q:
With reference to the two opinions in the Section 17A split verdict, consider the following statements:
1. Justice Viswanathan would have approval rest on a binding opinion of the Lokpal for Central employees and of the State Lokayukta for State employees.
2. Justice Nagarathna called the provision 'old wine in a new bottle', reviving what earlier rulings had struck down.
3. Justice Nagarathna found that the provision fails both intelligible differentia and rational nexus.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Justice Viswanathan kept Section 17A valid to protect honest officers and avoid a play-it-safe bureaucracy, but moved the filter from the government to an independent body under the 2013 Lokpal law. Justice Nagarathna held it unconstitutional under Article 14, seeing it as a return of the filters struck down in Vineet Narain and Subramanian Swamy. The matter has gone to a larger bench, so neither view is settled law.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6

questions.q:
In the context of India's anti-corruption framework, consider the following statements:
1. The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 allows inquiry into allegations against public functionaries, including the Prime Minister.
2. The UN Convention against Corruption is a legally binding treaty that India ratified in 2011.
3. The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 provides a framework to inquire into corruption complaints and protect complainants.
4. The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 covers offences under the PMLA and the PCA, among others.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. UNCAC is binding on its parties, and a careless reader might treat it as a soft declaration. The Lokpal Act's reach to the Prime Minister is a well-known feature. The whistle-blower law pairs inquiry into complaints with protection of complainants. The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act reaches beyond its name to scheduled offences including benami transactions and fraud. The wider framework also includes the RTI Act, 2005 and the CVC Act, 2003.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9

questions.q: 'Presumptive titling', blamed for much of India's land litigation, is best described as a system in which
o: land held for a fixed period without challenge automatically vests in the occupant
a Sub-Registrar decides ownership on registration, subject to appeal to the Collector
the State guarantees title and compensates anyone who loses by an error in the register
ownership is inferred from deeds, revenue receipts, mutation entries and possession, none of which is conclusive
questions.e: Under presumptive titling no single record is final, so ownership can always be challenged, which creates a heavy due-diligence burden and long litigation. A State-guaranteed register describes conclusive titling, the reform goal rather than the present position. Sub-Registrars do not decide ownership, as both Samiullah and K. Gopi stress. Vesting through long possession belongs to the law of limitation and adverse possession, and it does not define this system.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-23

questions.q:
With respect to the prior-approval rulings, consider the following statements:
1. Vineet Narain struck down a statutory provision enacted by Parliament that required prior approval.
2. Subramanian Swamy v. Director, CBI (2014) struck down Section 6A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act as violating Article 14.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Vineet Narain struck down an executive instrument, the 'Single Directive', and not an Act of Parliament. Parliament later put a similar filter into statute as Section 6A, covering officers of Joint Secretary rank and above. The Court held in 2014 that this class could not be given special protection. So the difference between the cases is the kind of instrument involved and the ground used.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6

questions.q:
In the context of the debate on the office of Governor, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal.
2. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
3. The Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions favoured consulting the State's Chief Minister on the appointment.
4. Article 356 makes a report of the Governor the sole basis on which President's Rule can be imposed.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 fails because Article 356 allows the President to act on the Governor's report or otherwise, so a report is not the only route. Articles 155 and 156 explain why the Governor is called the Centre's appointee: the term is five years, but subject to the President's pleasure. The two Commissions suggested consultation to reduce friction with elected State governments over practices such as the annual address.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4; Articles 155, 156 and 356 wording is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Governor's address under Article 176 is prepared by the State Council of Ministers.
Statement-II: Rules of procedure must allot time for discussing matters referred to in the address.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but they answer different questions. Statement-I is about who writes the speech, which follows from the Governor acting on ministerial advice. Statement-II is about what the House does afterwards, leading to a vote on the Motion of Thanks. The discussion rule does not explain who drafts the address. Such questions often pair two true statements, so always ask whether the second actually gives the reason for the first.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4

questions.q:
Match List-I (case) with List-II (principle):
List-I
A. Shamsher Singh (1974)
B. Nabam Rebia (2016)
C. Meghraj Kothari (1966)
D. Gurmit Singh (1996)
List-II
1. A victim's testimony is not to be doubted because of alleged 'loose morals'
2. The Governor is a constitutional head acting on ministerial advice
3. The bar on courts in delimitation matters was meant to avoid delaying elections
4. The address under Articles 175 and 176 is performed on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Shamsher Singh set out the general principle that the Governor acts on ministerial advice. Nabam Rebia applied it specifically to the address, so the two are easily swapped because they point in the same direction. Meghraj Kothari is the delimitation case, which also preceded the 2024 Rathod ruling. Gurmit Singh belongs to the law on sexual offences and also holds prior sexual history irrelevant.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4; Vision IAS pp. 5-7; Shankar IAS pp. 8-9

questions.q:
With reference to Census 2027, consider the following statements:
1. Population enumeration in Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand is scheduled for September 2026.
2. Caste was last fully enumerated in the Census of 1951.
3. It will be the first census since Independence to record caste in any form.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Caste was last fully enumerated in 1931, so statement 2 fails. Statement 3 fails because Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes have already been counted in censuses after Independence. What is new is a nationwide caste count for all communities. House-listing runs from April to September 2026 in all States and UTs, and enumeration elsewhere takes place in February 2027.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15

questions.q:
With reference to how seats are allocated in legislatures abroad, consider the following statements:
1. In the European Parliament, the population represented per seat rises as a member State's population rises.
2. The size of the US House of Representatives has stayed at 435 since 1913, and seats move among States after each Census by the method of equal proportion.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The European Parliament has 720 members across 27 States, and under degressive proportionality larger States get more seats overall but fewer per head. The US keeps its total fixed and moves seats between States, so faster-growing States gain at the expense of others, even though its population has grown more than threefold since. The models show different choices: Europe protects smaller States by design, while the US follows population within a fixed total.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7

questions.q:
In the context of the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Executive Committee posts are reserved to ensure at least four women members.
2. The National Sports Election Panel must have at least 20 members at all times.
3. Disqualification applies to persons sentenced to life imprisonment but not to those given shorter terms.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: disqualification is stated for persons convicted and sentenced to imprisonment, and it is not confined to life terms. The Rules were notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, along with separate Rules for the National Sports Board's selection committee. The General Body provisions on Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit are a separate requirement from the Executive Committee's reserved posts.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13

questions.q: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission's suggestion on State anti-corruption machinery, cited in the debate on corruption, was to
o: bring Anti-Corruption Bureaus under the State Vigilance Commission
place Anti-Corruption Bureaus under the State Home Department
merge Anti-Corruption Bureaus with the Central Bureau of Investigation
replace Anti-Corruption Bureaus with Lokayukta benches
questions.e: The Commission wanted Anti-Corruption Bureaus placed under the State Vigilance Commission, along with stronger State economic-offences units and a code of ethics for public officials. Merging with the CBI would raise federal problems because police is a State subject. Placing them under the Home Department would not add independence, and replacing them with Lokayukta benches was not its proposal. The aim was stronger vigilance within the State machinery.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9

questions.q:
With reference to reports cited in the debates on corruption and urban water, consider the following pairs:
Report or analysis : Publisher
1. Corruption Perception Index : Transparency International
2. Analysis of undisclosed party funding : Association for Democratic Reforms
3. Composite Water Management Index : NITI Aayog
4. Pey Jal Survekshan : Ministry of Jal Shakti
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 4 is wrong because Pey Jal Survekshan is run under AMRUT 2.0, which belongs to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. The Jal Shakti Ministry is the tempting answer because of its name. Transparency International ranks perceived public-sector corruption. ADR reviews contributions to political parties. NITI Aayog's 2018 index projected that 21 major cities would run out of groundwater.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-11

questions.q: 'Intelligible differentia' and 'rational nexus', relied on in the Section 17A verdict, are the two limbs of the
o: test of proportionality for restrictions under Article 19
test of reasonable classification under Article 14
questions.e: Article 14 permits classification only if the group is separated on an intelligible differentia and that differentia has a rational nexus with the law's object. Proportionality, manifest arbitrariness and severability are real constitutional doctrines, but they do different work and are not built from these two limbs. Justice Nagarathna held that Section 17A fails this classification test because it shields one class of public servants.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6; test wording is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Delimitation Commission, consider the following statements:
1. A Commission has been constituted after every decennial census since Independence.
2. Neither the Lok Sabha nor a State Assembly can modify the Commission's orders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Commissions were set up four times, in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002, so there was none after the 1981, 1991 or 2011 censuses, which is why statement 1 fails. The orders have the force of law and take effect on a date specified by the President, and legislatures cannot alter them, although courts can now review manifestly arbitrary orders after the 2024 Rathod ruling.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7; census gap is static

questions.q:
In the light of Samiullah v. State of Bihar and K. Gopi v. Sub-Registrar (2025), consider the following statements:
1. Registration of a sale deed creates only a rebuttable presumption of ownership.
2. Sub-Registrars may refuse registration if they find the seller's title doubtful after a quasi-judicial inquiry.
3. Rules made under delegated power cannot expand the scope of the parent Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: registering officers perform a ministerial function, checking identity, property description and formalities, while title disputes go to civil courts. The Bihar rules demanding proof of mutation failed because they exceeded the Registration Act, 1908, and K. Gopi struck down a similar Tamil Nadu rule demanding the original title deed.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 21-23; K. Gopi year corrected from 2025 INSC 462

questions.q:
With reference to the age of consent and child protection law, consider the following statements:
1. The Justice Verma Committee recommended raising the age of consent from 16 to 18 years.
2. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita treats specified sexual acts with a woman under 18 as rape, with or without her consent.
3. The POCSO Act, 2012 protects girl children alone.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Justice Verma Committee recommended keeping the age at 16, and Parliament raised it to 18 in the 2013 Amendment, so statement 1 fails. POCSO is gender-neutral, so statement 3 fails. The age of consent is separate from the marriage age under the 2006 Act, which is 18 for females and 21 for males. Each of these provisions must be recalled separately.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 15; Shankar IAS pp. 6-8

questions.q:
With reference to the Bindra Task Force's recommendations, consider the following statements:
1. The National Council for Sports Education and Capacity Building is proposed as an advisory body without statutory backing.
2. The National Competency Framework envisages a career pathway from district to global level through a Five-Level Capability Maturity Model.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Council is proposed as an autonomous statutory body under the Sports Ministry, with power to regulate, accredit and certify all sports-administration training, so statement 1 fails. Its operational arm would be the National Training and Development Cell. The competency framework would run from district through State, national and institutional levels to global. Performance management would evaluate administrators as rigorously as athletes.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court urged the Centre to consider a 'Romeo-Juliet' clause.
Statement-II: Because consent below 18 has no legal value under POCSO, genuine adolescent relationships can attract prosecution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The bright line of 18 is what brings such relationships within the Act, and the Court also flagged misrepresented ages and families using the law against young couples. A close-in-age clause would exempt relationships with a minimal age difference. The law's supporters reply that a clear line protects children from coercion hidden behind claims of consent.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 15; Shankar IAS pp. 6-8

questions.q:
Which of the following are counted as Non-Revenue Water?
1. Treated water lost through pipeline leaks
2. Water theft
3. Water delivered to consumers but not billed because of billing errors
4. Treated wastewater reused for non-potable purposes
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Non-Revenue Water is treated water that produces no revenue. It includes physical losses such as leaks and apparent losses such as theft, unmetered use and billing errors. Wastewater reuse is a separate conservation measure, so item 4 does not belong. About 38 per cent of India's water supply is lost this way, so water audits and leak detection are part of the way forward.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
In the context of the age-of-consent debate, consider the following statements:
1. The 240th Standing Committee Report (2011) rejected recognising minors' consent in the POCSO Bill.
2. The 167th Standing Committee Report (2013) supported a close-in-age exemption.
3. The Age of Consent Act, 1891 raised the age from 10 to 12 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 167th Report dealt with raising the age to 18, and Shankar records it as opposing any close-in-age exemption. Parliamentary bodies have consistently resisted lowering the age, so the proposal now under debate is an exemption for close-in-age relationships. The 1891 Act is the historical starting point, with IPC Section 375 later setting 16 before the 2012-13 changes moved the line to 18.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 6-8; 167th Report date corrected from PRS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988:
Statement-I: Justice Nagarathna reasoned that Section 17A is not needed to protect honest public servants.
Statement-II: Section 19 already requires sanction before a public servant is prosecuted in court.
Statement-III: Section 19 applies at the stage before any inquiry or investigation begins.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that one explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct, and II gives her reasoning: honest officers already have protection at the prosecution stage. Statement-III is wrong because it describes Section 17A, which requires approval before inquiry or investigation into official recommendations or decisions. Section 19 operates later. Keeping the two stages apart is the essential point, since the safeguards are often mixed up in news reports.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6

questions.q:
After the Indore contamination crisis, consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission:
1. It can take suo motu cognizance of a human rights violation.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the government concerned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Commission can inquire on its own motion, on a petition or on a court's direction, and in Indore it found the main pipeline ran beneath a public toilet. Its recommendations carry moral and public weight but are not binding in themselves, so statement 2 fails. The government concerned must report what action it has taken.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-11; Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Purely population-based delimitation could reduce the relative Lok Sabha share of States that stabilised their population.
Statement-II: Article 82 of the Constitution bars any readjustment of constituencies after a census.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is the southern States' concern, since high-growth States such as Uttar Pradesh and Bihar would gain share. Statement-II is wrong: Article 82 provides for readjustment after each census, by an authority and in a manner Parliament decides. Its provisos only freeze the inter-State allocation for a period. So the Constitution requires realignment in principle, and the political dispute is about when and on what formula it should resume.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7; the freeze is static; the 131st Bill is after January

questions.q:
Which of the following statements about anti-trafficking measures are correct?
1. Operation AAHT and Operation Nanhe Farishtey are Railway Protection Force operations.
2. The UJJAWALA Scheme covers prevention, rescue, rehabilitation, reintegration and repatriation of trafficked women and children.
3. Anti-Human Trafficking Units are specialised district police units.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are correct. Since police and law and order are State subjects, these measures depend on Union-State coordination. UJJAWALA is now being merged into Shakti Sadans under Mission Shakti. Railway operations matter because trafficking networks rely on transit, and rehabilitation schemes address what happens after rescue. District units are the local investigating arm that links the two.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11; RPF point is a static anchor in the notes; merger from WCD FAQs

questions.q:
With respect to the ranks specified in clauses (a) to (c) of Section 17 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, consider the following pairs:
1. Delhi Special Police Establishment : Deputy Superintendent of Police
2. Metropolitan areas such as Bombay and Madras : Assistant Commissioner of Police
3. Other areas : Deputy Superintendent of Police or equivalent
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 1 is wrong because clause (a) specifies Inspector for the Delhi Special Police Establishment. These ranks apply to investigation without a magistrate's order and to arrest without a warrant. A proviso also lets a State Government authorise an officer of Inspector rank or above, so these are the specified ranks, not an absolute floor. Anyone below these ranks needs specific authorisation.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6; Section 17 proviso checked against the Act

questions.q: Which one of the following about the long-pending projects associated with PRAGATI is correct?
o: The Bogibeel rail-cum-road bridge unlocked through it lies over the Ganga
An Oxford Said Business School study described it as a global benchmark and a 'single source of truth'
Its review meetings are limited to Union Secretaries
The Jammu-Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla rail link was approved in 2014 and commissioned in 2020
questions.e: The Oxford study is the correct claim, praising real-time project monitoring. Bogibeel lies over the Brahmaputra, not the Ganga. The rail link was approved in 1994 and commissioned in 2025, and Navi Mumbai International Airport is another cited project. Review meetings bring together Union Secretaries and State Chief Secretaries under the Prime Minister's chairmanship, which is why PRAGATI is cited as cooperative federalism.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 13-16; river is static

questions.q:
In the context of the Governor's role in the legislature, consider the following pairs:
Article : Subject
1. Article 159 : Oath or affirmation by the Governor
2. Article 176 : Governor's address at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year
3. Article 201 : President's action on a Bill reserved by the Governor
4. Article 213 : Governor's giving or withholding of assent to Bills
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Pair 4 is wrong because Article 213 is the Governor's power to promulgate Ordinances. Giving or withholding assent, or reserving a Bill, falls under Article 200, and Article 201 takes over once the Bill reaches the President. Article 175 is the separate, discretionary power to address the House, which is why it should not be confused with the mandatory address under Article 176.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4, 11-13; Articles 200, 201 and 213 are static

questions.q:
With reference to child protection data reported in January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. In 2025, new POCSO filings exceeded case disposals.
2. The conviction rate in child trafficking cases during 2018-22 was above 50 per cent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. POCSO recorded 80,320 new cases and 87,754 disposals in 2025, a 109 per cent disposal rate and the first time disposals exceeded filings, helped by about 400 fast-track courts. Statement 2 is far off: the conviction rate was 4.8 per cent, which is the main enforcement gap. Better disposal in POCSO cases does not by itself mean better outcomes in trafficking cases.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
With reference to urban water schemes, consider the following statements:
1. AMRUT 2.0 promotes rainwater harvesting through storm-water drains into water bodies.
2. Aquifer Management Plans are part of AMRUT 2.0.
3. Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban) targets tap water supply in census villages.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban) covers all 4,378 statutory towns, not villages. AMRUT 2.0 links rainwater harvesting with groundwater recharge, so supply is treated with the aquifer in view. The Non-Revenue Water problem and scheme coverage are separate questions: schemes extend supply, while audits and leak detection reduce loss.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
With reference to disputes over the Governor's address, consider the following pairs:
State : Reported conduct of the Governor
1. Karnataka : Delivered a two-line speech and left the joint session
2. Kerala : Skipped some portions of the Cabinet-prepared address
3. Tamil Nadu : Has refused to deliver the Article 176 speech since 2024, even walking out
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Together they show the same dispute in different forms: partial reading, a token speech and refusal. The objection in each case is that the Governor is performing a constitutional duty and reading the elected government's text, so this conduct sits badly with the Article 159 oath and with Supreme Court rulings such as Nabam Rebia. Careless reading tends to swap Kerala and Karnataka.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 3-4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Urban water supply in India is mainly a State and municipal responsibility.
Statement-II: 'Water' is an entry in the State List, and water supply for domestic, industrial and commercial purposes is listed in the Twelfth Schedule.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Entry 17 of the State List covers water, subject to Entry 56 of the Union List on inter-State rivers and river valleys. The 74th Amendment, through the Twelfth Schedule, gave municipalities a wide mandate including water supply. So the Union mainly funds and guides through schemes such as AMRUT, which is why the Indore outbreak was read as a local governance failure.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-11; schedule and entry numbers are static

questions.q:
The Kerala language debate raised the constitutional scheme on language. Consider the following pairs:
Article : Provision
1. Article 351 : Directive for the development of the Hindi language
2. Article 345 : Language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts
3. Article 346 : Language for communication between States, and between a State and the Union
4. Article 350 : Language to be used in representations for redress of grievances
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Pair 2 is wrong because Article 345 lets a State Legislature adopt one or more official languages, which is the basis for Kerala's Bill, while Article 348 governs the language of the higher courts. That difference matters here, since the Bill only promises phased translation of judgments. A State's choice must also respect minority protections and central laws such as the Official Language Act, 1963.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 11-13; Articles 346, 348, 350 and 351 are static

questions.q:
With respect to Kerala's Malayalam Language Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Article 343 enables a State Legislature to adopt by law one or more languages for official purposes.
2. Before this Bill, both Malayalam and English were official languages of Kerala.
3. Karnataka's objection focuses on Kannada speakers, especially in Kasaragod.
4. Objections to Kerala's 2015 language Bill included inconsistency with the RTE Act, 2009.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 cites the wrong Article: Article 345 deals with State official languages, while Article 343 concerns the official language of the Union. The Bill would make Malayalam the sole official language. The 2015 Bill was reserved for the President and assent was withheld, with objections also citing the Official Language Act, 1963 and the Three-Language Formula.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 11-13; Article 345 is a static anchor in the notes

questions.q:
With reference to the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, consider the following statements:
1. Any Judge falls within the definition of 'public servant'.
2. A public duty is one in whose discharge the government, the public or the community has an interest.
3. Punishment for a habitual offender is higher than that for a public servant taking undue advantage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The range is 3 to 7 years for a public servant taking undue advantage and 5 to 10 years for a habitual offender, in each case with a fine. The wide definition also covers anyone empowered to perform adjudicatory functions and anyone holding an office that requires a public duty. These definitions matter because the Act's reach, and therefore Section 17A's protection, depends on who counts as a public servant.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; Shankar IAS pp. 4-6

questions.q:
In the context of the law on child trafficking, consider the following pairs:
Provision : Content
1. Article 39(e) and (f) : Fundamental Rights of children enforceable under Article 32
2. Article 23 : Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
3. Section 143, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita : Selling and buying of minors
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 2 is correct. Article 39(e) and (f) are Directive Principles, which courts cannot enforce directly. Section 143 of the BNS is the general trafficking offence, whereas Sections 98 and 99 cover selling and buying minors. Article 24 bars child employment in hazardous work. In K.P. Kiran Kumar (2025), the Court also linked child trafficking to Article 21, adding a right-to-life dimension.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11; enforceability is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Delimitation Commission of 2002 redrew constituency boundaries without changing the number of Lok Sabha seats held by each State.
Statement-II: The 84th Amendment permitted readjustment within States while keeping the inter-State allocation frozen until the first census after 2026.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The freeze separates two things: how many seats a State has, and how they are drawn inside it. The last Commission could only do the second, using 2001 figures after the 87th Amendment. So population shifts since 1971 have never altered State shares, which is why the next census carries such political weight for States that stabilised their population.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7; amendment history is static

questions.q:
With respect to the law on adolescent consent, consider the following statements:
1. The 283rd Law Commission Report (2023) advised against lowering the age of consent.
2. In In Re: Right to Privacy of Adolescents, the Supreme Court restored a POCSO conviction in 2024 and in 2025 used Article 142 to withhold sentence, in an order it said is not a precedent.
3. Section 19 of the POCSO Act places the duty to report an offence on doctors and teachers but not on other persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Section 19 applies to anyone who knows of or suspects an offence, who must report to the local police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit. The Article 142 order was fact-specific, so it did not change the statutory bright line of 18 years. The debate now turns on a possible close-in-age exemption, described as a 3-4 year gap for ages 16 to 18 with mandatory judicial review.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 6-8; Article 142 dates corrected from SC Observer

questions.q:
Regarding the Election Commission's ECINET platform, consider the following statements:
1. Its beta version was piloted during the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections.
2. The Election Commission's authority over elections, which the platform serves, comes from Article 326.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Commission's superintendence, direction and control of elections comes from Article 324. Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage, which makes these two Articles easy to confuse. ECINET was launched at IICDEM 2026 and brings services such as voter registration, electoral-roll search, Know Your Candidate, e-EPIC download and grievance redressal onto one platform.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 16; Article 326 is static

questions.q:
With reference to delimitation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Delimitation Commission orders take effect on a date specified by the Election Commission of India.
2. Article 82 governs the division of a State into Assembly constituencies, while Article 170 governs Lok Sabha constituencies.
3. Article 332 relates to the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in State Assemblies.
4. Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod (2024) held that manifestly arbitrary Commission orders can be reviewed by constitutional courts.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong because the date is specified by the President. Statement 2 reverses the Articles: Article 82 covers Lok Sabha constituencies and Article 170 covers Assembly constituencies. Article 330 is the Lok Sabha counterpart of Article 332. Commission orders have the force of law and neither the Lok Sabha nor an Assembly can modify them, but the 2024 ruling keeps judicial review open for manifestly arbitrary orders.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 5-7

questions.q:
In the context of sports administration, consider the following statements:
1. Kirsty Coventry, first woman President of the International Olympic Committee, is cited in the context of the Task Force's Dual Athlete Career Pathway.
2. e-Khel Pathshala is a digital platform of the Sports Authority of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. The Pathway combines performance with leadership education and a 'Sportsman of Merit' certification. e-Khel Pathshala trains teachers and community coaches at the grassroots, and the Task Force wants it overseen by a National Training and Development Cell. The core finding is that India has no professional cadre of sports administrators, and these measures respond to that gap on the way to the 2036 goals.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13

questions.q:
With reference to governance portals launched recently, consider the following statements:
1. The Glossary of Revenue Terms was launched under the National Monetisation Pipeline.
2. The PANKHUDI portal is a single-window CSR platform of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
3. Land Stack is a blockchain ledger of property records modelled on Estonia's practice.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The Glossary was launched with Land Stack under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme. PANKHUDI belongs to the Ministry of Women and Child Development, though its CSR focus makes the Corporate Affairs Ministry a tempting guess. Land Stack is a GIS-based platform modelled on practices in Singapore, the UK and Finland. Blockchain was a separate suggestion made by the Court in Samiullah.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 13-16

questions.q:
With reference to Supreme Court rulings on child exploitation, consider the following pairs:
Case : Subject
1. Vishal Jeet v. Union of India (1990) : Guidelines on child employment in hazardous industries
2. M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) : Trafficking and child prostitution
3. Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011) : Directions against child exploitation and trafficking
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is correct, since the first two are swapped. Vishal Jeet treated trafficking and child prostitution as socio-economic problems needing a preventive, humane approach. M.C. Mehta laid down guidelines on child employment in hazardous industries, building on Article 24. The third case, Bachpan Bachao Andolan, gave directions against widespread child exploitation and trafficking.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
With reference to legal safeguards for victims of sexual offences, consider the following statements:
1. Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita prohibits disclosure of the identity of a victim of sexual assault.
2. The Supreme Court's bar on naming victims extends to deceased victims, unless a competent authority decides otherwise.
3. State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh (1996) treated a victim's prior sexual history as irrelevant.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Section 72 replaced Section 228A of the IPC. The 2018 and 2019 directions cover deceased victims, subject to the decision of a competent authority. Gurmit Singh also affirmed that every woman can refuse intercourse. The wider point in the recent debate is that public shaming by officials can amount to a 'second crime' even when the identity bar is not technically breached.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 8-9

questions.q:
With reference to the law on trafficking, consider the following statements:
1. The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 addresses trafficking for sexual exploitation.
2. Under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, the trafficking definition applies if the victim did not consent, but not otherwise.
3. The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 covers the care, protection and rehabilitation of child victims.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is the wrong one, because the 2013 definition applies irrespective of consent. It covers sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal, which matters since coercion in trafficking is often hidden. Statements 1 and 3 correctly describe the two other Acts. The Supreme Court's K.P. Kiran Kumar ruling upheld a conviction under the ITPA and asked courts to treat minors' testimony with sensitivity.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 9-11

questions.q:
With reference to sports governance reforms, consider the following statements:
1. The Task Force on Capacity Building of Sports Administrators was constituted under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
2. The Search-cum-Selection Committee for the National Sports Board is chaired by the Chief Justice of India.
3. A national sports body's General Body must include at least four Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit, all of whom must be women.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The Bindra Task Force was constituted under Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, while the 2025 Act is the basis of the later Rules. The Cabinet Secretary chairs the committee, and its other members are the Sports Secretary, a person experienced in sports administration and two national sports award recipients. Statement 3 fails because 50 per cent of those Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit must be women, not all, and they must be at least 25.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 12-13

questions.q:
With respect to the Malayalam Language Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Court judgments must be delivered in Malayalam immediately from the date of commencement.
2. Students from other States and foreign countries are exempt from Malayalam examinations in Classes 9, 10 and higher secondary.
3. Kerala's safeguards name Tamil, Kannada, Tulu and Konkani speakers.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is wrong, because judgments and proceedings are to be translated in a phased manner and not switched at once. Statements 2 and 3 describe Kerala's defence of the Bill. Linguistic minorities may also correspond in their mother tongues with the Secretariat, department heads and local offices in designated areas. The Bill also renames the Official Language Department and creates a new Directorate to oversee implementation.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 11-13
